validator: draft 1 passes validate.mjs with no problems, soft points or warnings.
keep: The idea is named in one line up front: each fact about the two unknowns is one equation, so two separate facts give two equations, and their pair fits the whole story.

One fully worked example with real numbers (the two cinema receipts, solved by substitution to a £3 drink and £2 popcorn, checked on both receipts), a second in the law of a machine with a and b as the unknowns, and a third in practice (the cable order), each checked in the story and read back with units.
OpenStax's steps [1] are taught in order: say what you are looking for, name each unknown with a letter, one equation per fact, solve, check in the story, say what it means.
The same-fact-twice receipt shows the special cases from lessons 1 and 2 in a story: doubled, the lines lie on top of each other [5]; a different total, they run parallel and nothing fits [3].

Thirteen screens alternate SHOW (0, 2, 4, 6, 8) and DO (1, 3, 5, 7, 9), ending on three mixed puzzles (10 substitution on lengths, 11 elimination on prices, 12 a machine's law used at a new load). Each brief mistake has a DO with its own hint: swapped letters (1, 3, 5, 7, 11), a count written as a sum (1), one fact only (3, 5, 10, 11), the same fact twice (9), the law forced through zero (7, 12), and the answer with no meaning (every Why? says what the pair means, with units).
The analogy is new for this course (two lighthouse bearings fixing a ship), reproduces the main result (one fact a line, two facts a point) and says where it breaks.
fix: Skipped causal step: explain says every accepted guess 'lands on one straight line' without saying why. Add it: for each drink price exactly one popcorn price makes the total, and each £1 more on the drink must come off as £2 less on the popcorn, a steady step, so the guesses fall on a straight line, as in Straight-line graphs.

Rule in words comes too late: 'each item's count times its price, added up, makes the total' is stated in paragraph 2, after paragraph 1 has already turned the receipt into 2 × d + p. Move it to where the first receipt becomes an equation.
False absolute: 'Dragging guesses about finds it' holds only when the answer sits on a grid mark. Say it finds it only one guess at a time, and only when the answer falls on a mark.
Misconception shown failing is missing from explain: show a guess that passes one receipt only, (£2, £4) making 2 + 8 = 10 on the second, not 7.
Practice's 'substitution when one fact already says what a letter equals, elimination otherwise' reads as a rule; make it 'usually'.

'Each fact a story gives about two unknowns becomes one equation' is wider than the course: in this course's stories each fact can be written as one straight-line equation. Narrow it to 'each fact ... can be written as one equation'.
